{"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{"listChanged":false},"resources":{"subscribe":false,"listChanged":false},"prompts":{"listChanged":false},"sampling":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"MockServer","version":"9.2.0"},"instructions":"MockServer is an HTTP(S) mock server and proxy for testing. Use these tools to mock APIs, debug failing requests, and verify implementations:
- Mock APIs: 'create_expectation', 'create_expectation_from_openapi', and 'create_expectations_from_recorded_traffic' (turn traffic already recorded via the proxy into mocks).
- Debug a request that did not match: call 'explain_unmatched_requests' after a failed test run to see, for each request that hit the server, the closest expectations ranked by similarity with field-level diffs and a remediation hint — no need to reconstruct the request. 'debug_request_mismatch' does the same for a request you supply. 'explain_request' takes one received request's correlation id (from 'retrieve_logs') and says which expectation serves it now and why each one ahead of it lost; 'diagnose_config' shows which settings are in effect and where they came from. 'suggest_expectation_fix' proposes a guarded JSON patch for each close expectation; 'lint_expectations' finds expectations that can never match; 'explain_forward_failure' says why a forward or proxied request got a 502; 'test_template' dry-runs a response or forward template.
- Verify an implementation: 'verify_request' / 'verify_request_sequence' check requests were made; 'verify_traffic_against_openapi' checks recorded traffic conforms to an OpenAPI contract; 'run_contract_test' sends spec-derived example requests to a running service and checks the responses; 'run_resiliency_test' sends malformed and boundary-case requests and reports which inputs the service failed to handle gracefully.
- Deterministic LLM testing: 'record_llm_fixtures' snapshots LLM/MCP traffic recorded through the proxy into a committable, secret-free fixture file; 'load_expectations_from_file' replays it.
Readable resources expose live state: mockserver://expectations, mockserver://requests, mockserver://logs, mockserver://unmatched, mockserver://configuration."}}

It is evaluated against the requests recorded now, so it also counts any that arrived after the original check ran. 3. If no request reached MockServer at all, call 'get_status' to confirm it is running and which ports it listens on, then call 'retrieve_logs' to look for errors.
Then say whether the code under test sent a different request, sent it a different number of times, or the verification itself expects the wrong thing, and suggest the change.

{"id":14,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"description":"Finds the smallest change that makes an existing MockServer expectation match a request, starting from the fix MockServer suggests, and applies it only once the user agrees","messages":[{"role":"user","content":{"type":"text","text":"A GET request to /orders/2 is not getting the response the user expects from MockServer. Work through these steps in order.
1. Call 'suggest_expectation_fix' with limit 20, adding "expectationId" if the user named the expectation they meant. It covers only requests that reached MockServer and matched nothing. Use only the entries in "unmatchedRequests" whose "method" and "path" are GET and /orders/2; each lists close expectations by "expectationId", each with a "suggestedFix": a "patch" (an RFC 6902 JSON patch of the expectation as 'list_expectations' returns it, each change preceded by a "test" of the current value), the "unpatchedFields" it could not patch with the reason for each, and "matchesAfterPatch". Nothing is applied.
2. Call 'list_expectations' and take the full JSON of the expectation the user meant (normally the first one with a suggested fix) by its id.
3. If there is no suggested fix for that expectation (a "suggestedFixCount" of 0 with a "note" means the request may not have been sent or may have matched another expectation; a fix is suggested only for the five closest expectations), or its "matchesAfterPatch" is false, or "unpatchedFields" lists fields, call 'debug_request_mismatch' with method "GET" and path "/orders/2", adding the request's headers and body if the user gave them. It returns one result per active expectation, closest first, each with its "expectationId", whether it "matches", the "differences" per field and a "remediation" hint. If an expectation the user did not mean also matches, it may be the one answering the request: say so.
Propose the change: the suggested patch applied to the expectation's JSON when there is one, plus the smallest hand-made change to any field it left unpatched, or only a hand-made change when no fix was suggested. Show each changed field with its old and new value and say which changes MockServer suggested. Do not apply it until the user agrees. Then call 'raw_expectation' with the corrected expectation, keeping its "id" so it replaces the original rather than adding a second one, and call 'debug_request_mismatch' again to confirm that it now matches.

Answer in two separate sections. Under the heading "Facts from MockServer", list only values copied from the tool results (status codes, counts, field names, differences and error text), each with the name of the tool that returned it, without rewording them. If a tool returned an error or nothing, say so there instead of guessing. Under the heading "Interpretation", give your explanation and the change you suggest, and present nothing in that section as MockServer output."}}]}}

{"id":15,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"description":"Explains why MockServer could not forward or proxy a request, from the failed forwards MockServer recorded and the forward expectation","messages":[{"role":"user","content":{"type":"text","text":"A GET request to /orders/2 that MockServer should have forwarded or proxied failed. Work through these steps in order.
1. Call 'explain_forward_failure' with limit 20. It returns "forwardFailures", most recent first, each with its "correlationId", "method", "path", "statusCode" (502) and "reason"; use the ones whose method and path are GET and /orders/2. When "causeNamed" is true, the reason is the cause MockServer named and what to change (for example a TLS failure, an HTTP/2 error, a connection it could not set up, an upstream response it could not decode, an unresolvable host, or a refused or timed-out connection), and it is also the 502 body. When "forwardLoopSuspected" is true, the forward went back to MockServer itself. When "causeNamed" is false, the reason is the raw error: call 'retrieve_logs' with that "correlationId" to see the request's whole lifecycle, including any exception logged for it.
2. Call 'list_expectations' with path "/orders/2" to find the expectation that forwarded it and note its target host, port and scheme. If none matches, MockServer was acting as a proxy and sent the request to the host the request itself named.
3. If "forwardFailureCount" is 0, or no failure has this method and path, call 'retrieve_request_responses' with method "GET" and path "/orders/2" to see what MockServer sent back: a response other than a 502 means the forward did not fail inside MockServer. MockServer records failed forwards only when its logLevel is INFO or more detailed (the default is INFO), and drops the oldest log entries beyond maxLogEntries, so if neither tool shows the request, report that instead of guessing a cause.
Then name the most likely cause and the change to make: to the forward target, the upstream service, MockServer's TLS or proxy settings, or the network between them.
